title: John Chrysostom on Luke 1:2
body: “Knowing therefore this, let us continue steadfastly to hold what "they have delivered unto us, which from the beginning were eye-witnesses, and ministers of the word." ( Luke i.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on Luke 1:2
body: “The former treatise have I made, O Theophilus, of all that Jesus began both to do and to teach." (v.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans

title: John Chrysostom on Luke 1:3
body: “The former treatise have I made, O Theophilus, of all that Jesus began both to do and to teach." (v.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans

title: John Chrysostom on Luke 1:4
body: “But now consider the benevolent and Apostolic feelings of the writer: that for the sake of a single individual he took such pains as to write for him an entire Gospel. "That thou mightest have," he says, "the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed." (Luke i.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans

title: Augustine on Luke 2:52
body: “It was the doctrine of Paul of Samosata, that the man Christ was exalted to be the Son of God (prokope, from Luke ii.”
author: Augustine, Homilies on the Gospels

title: John Chrysostom on Luke 10:22
body: “Christ says in another place, "No one knoweth who the Son is, save the Father; and who the Father is, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son willeth to reveal Him." (Luke x.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on Luke 10:24
body: “How then," says one, "did He say Himself, Many prophets have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them'?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on Luke 14:11
body: “For as in bodies it is one thing to be healthy and plump, (sphrigonta, firm and elastic.) and another thing to be swoln, although both indicate a full habit of flesh, (but in this case of unsound, in that of healthful flesh;) so also here: it is one thing to be arrogant, which is, as it were, to be swoln, and another thing to be high-souled, which is to be in a healthy state.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on Luke 15:7
body: “And now then behold the fruit. He straightway recompensed them with his carnal things. "He brought them up into his house, and set meat before them, and rejoiced greatly with all his house, having believed in God." For what was he not ready to do, now that by the opening of the prison doors, heaven itself was opened to him?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on Luke 18:13
body: “Wouldest thou know how good our Master is? The Publican went up full of ten thousand wickednesses, and saying only, "Be merciful unto me," went down justified.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on Luke 18:19
body: “This text has various interpretations. S. Athanasius uses it to imply that God, as Father of the Son, is the only true Father, and that all created paternity is a shadow of the true.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on Luke 20:42
body: “And the world knew Him not." By "the world" he here means the multitude, which is corrupt, and closely attached to earthly things, the common turbulent, silly people.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on Luke 22:35
body: “But prove to me that Peter and Paul were eloquent. Thou canst not: for they were "unlearned and ignorant men!" As therefore Christ, when He was sending out His disciples into the world, having shewn unto them His power in Palestine first, and said, (St.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
